title: My Cursor Vibe Jam game is finally live!
author: u3030
selftext:
Close to the end of the 2026 Cursor Vibe Jam, I finally submitted my game: We Die Below

[http://wediebelow.app/](http://wediebelow.app/)



We Die Below is a single-player or 1–4 player co-op dungeon battler inspired at least in part by Gauntlet, Diablo, maybe a little Helldivers..

A quick technical note: mobile "works" but the game relies pretty heavily on WebGPU, so results may vary depending on your device. For the best experience, I recommend playing on a PC with mouse/keyboard. If you’re on a laptop, you may also need to make sure your browser is using your dedicated GPU and not the integrated GPU.

A lot of the build was done through Claude Code, with me integrating and iterating directly in the Claude Code console. For assets, I used a combination of local Trellis and the Meshy API, then rigged and animated characters using ComfyUI, Blender MCP, and a few other tools (ChatGPT for some good AI flavoring).



Some tools I found especially useful while building:

Make It Animatable

[https://huggingface.co/spaces/jasongzy/Make-It-Animatable](https://huggingface.co/spaces/jasongzy/Make-It-Animatable)

This can be installed locally and used to rig humanoid characters.

HY Motion

[https://github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/HY-Motion-1.0](https://github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/HY-Motion-1.0)

Useful for creating animations for rigged humanoid characters via prompts.



I also followed a lot of the workflow outlined here, and highly recommend the channel in general:

[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qjcNLLbtIEs](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qjcNLLbtIEs)



If you play it, I hope you enjoy it as much as we enjoyed building it.



I’m also planning to port We Die Below to Unity for a Steam release later this year, with revamped assets, effects, and fewer HTML deployment constraints:

[https://store.steampowered.com/app/4662150/We\_Die\_Below/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4662150/We_Die_Below/)

comments.author: stellarton
comments.body:
Congrats on shipping it. Getting a playable game out of a jam is already hard, and adding AI-assisted workflow on top makes it extra interesting.

I’d be curious what Cursor helped with most: gameplay logic, debugging, refactoring, UI/polish, or just moving faster through boilerplate?

Also, did the WebGPU/mobile limitation come up late, or was that something you knew you’d have to work around from the start?

replies.author: u3030
replies.body:
Thanks!  

I didn't use Cursor, they're just the game jam main sponsor.  Most of the AI assist centered around Claude Code, using it to scaffold up everything youu described, as well as developing a set of custom workflows to speed up development and asset production. 

It did pretty well, apart from making the occasional bad assumption.  I found very clear, detailed requirements and bug reports were key.   Its sort of like having an overly confident full stack developer on hand.  

For the WebGPU issue, we'd always planned on using it.  The issue came up during testing, we found several laptops, even ones with advanced GPUs (my wife's has a 4090) played it like a potato because they were defaulting to the integrated graphics cards in the browser.  And we weren't really targeting mobile, but wanted it to at least be playable on low-quality settings.

comments.author: Revelation12Studios
comments.body: For future work, I suggest to get some different colors for the rooms. Everything kind of looks like the exact same color.

replies.author: u3030
replies.body: Yeah I definitely plan on making a lot of changes on my way to the Unity build. Effects, higher quality characters, more interesting levels, etc..  This was more like a mad dash to get something built 😁

comments.author: MedivalBlacksmith
comments.body: It's very dark. Add some lighting. 😎

replies.author: u3030
replies.body: Yeah fair, I got into a bit of a hole where the lighting was causing performance problems so I scaled them back, maybe a bit too much 😃
